problem: The current webpack/Sass URL-rebasing gap remains documented by sass-loader and used by active projects, while the sole-writer package has had no v5 release since 2022 and has unresolved Windows-path and maintenance issues.
successorLandscape: No current general-purpose maintained npm drop-in was found. Next.js vendors a tailored implementation, and current sass-loader documentation still recommends resolve-url-loader for this exact problem.
compatibilityContract: Preserve the callable CommonJS webpack loader, Object.assign join helpers, packed deep lib entries, webpack 4/5 behavior, string/object source maps, source-relative/project-relative formats, custom join semantics, query/hash retention, Windows/POSIX paths, Node >=12, and legacy-key npm alias installation.
risk: Source-map/path behavior is cross-platform and filesystem-sensitive; dependency modernization and Windows file-URL normalization can silently change emitted CSS or source maps.
maintenanceCost: high: real webpack 4/5 builds, current and historical Sass pipelines, Windows/POSIX behavior, malformed maps, custom iterators, and packed consumer matrices must remain covered.
proofOfSuccess: Differential upstream parity plus an issue-239 Windows regression, clean webpack 4/5 and current Dart Sass builds, Node 12-24 and Windows CI, TypeScript 3.9/current declarations, zero-finding production audit, exact Verdaccio/npm artifact verification, and one independently tested downstream migration.
